DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no human biological father

**Position.** No man begat Jesus. Mary conceived him of the Holy Ghost, and Joseph was husband to Mary but not the one who begat him. [L4, resting on the layers below]

## 1. Mary was a virgin when she conceived

[L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."
[L2] The Greek is *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin." Luke applies it twice to Mary in one verse.

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L2] The Greek is *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know," here of sexual knowledge. *Aner* (G435) means "a man" as male, and Mary says she knows none.
[L3] Genesis 4:1 uses the Hebrew counterpart, *yada* (H3045), "to know," in the same sense: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain."

[L4] Mary's question concerns how she could conceive without sexual knowledge of a man. Luke 1:27 and Genesis 4:1 supply the two footings: Luke calls her a virgin, and "know" is the verb of conception between husband and wife. Her statement of not knowing a man therefore excludes a male begetter at the time of the announcement.

## 2. The source of the conception is the Holy Ghost, not a man

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] The Greek *ek* (G1537) means "out of," marking source or origin. *Pneuma hagion* is "Holy Spirit." The conception is "out of" the Holy Ghost, and the verse says it happened "before they came together."

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] The Greek for "conceived" is *gennaō* (G1080), "to beget" or "to be begotten." Matthew uses the same verb for the fathers. [L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac." Where a man is the source, the line says "begat." Where Jesus is concerned, the same verb names the Holy Ghost as the source.

[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] *Episkiazō* (G1982) means "to overshadow." The angel names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest as the agent. Joseph is not named.

[L4] Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 give the source as the Holy Ghost, through *ek* and *gennaō*. [L3] Matthew 1:2 shows that *gennaō* is the begetting verb elsewhere in the same chapter. Luke 1:35 gives "therefore," the reason Jesus is called the Son of God. The reason is the Holy Ghost's act, not any man's.

## 3. The genealogy breaks the pattern at Joseph

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
[L2] Every earlier line reads "begat" (*egennēsen*, from G1080). The last does not. Joseph is called "the husband" (*anēr*, G435, "man"), not the one who begat Jesus. The relative "of whom" (*ex hēs*) is feminine singular, so the birth is "out of her," meaning Mary.
[L3] Matthew 1:15: "and Matthan begat Jacob." The pattern runs unbroken to Jacob and Joseph, then turns to Mary.

[L4] The pattern is "X begat Y" throughout, and Matthew 1:16 changes it at one point. The verse and the feminine relative show that the birth is traced through Mary, not through Joseph's begetting.

## 4. Joseph's own understanding and the people's supposition

[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
[L3] Matthew 1:20 follows: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L4] Joseph's intent to put her away shows that he did not regard the child as his own. Matthew 1:20 answers him by naming a different source, and he receives it.

[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
[L2] *Ginōskō* (G1097) is again "knew" in the sexual sense, now of Joseph, so the sense matches Luke 1:34.

[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
[L2] *Nomizō* (G3543) means "to think, to suppose," a view held by others. Luke records that the opinion was a supposition.
[L3] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Mary uses the word "father" in the household sense. Jesus answers at Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" He names a different Father.

[L4] Luke 3:23 marks Joseph's fatherhood as supposed. Luke 2:48-49 shows two uses of "father" in one exchange, Mary's for Joseph and Jesus's for another. Matthew 1:25 limits Joseph's knowing of Mary to after the birth.

## 5. Prophecy and the prepared body

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
[L2] The Hebrew behind "virgin" is *almah* (H5959).
[L3] Genesis 24:43 uses *almah* for Rebekah ("when the virgin cometh forth to draw water"), and Genesis 24:16 describes the same Rebekah: "a virgin, neither had any man known her."
[L1] Matthew 1:23 quotes it: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son... God with us."
[L2] *Parthenos* (G3933) is "virgin."

[L1] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me."
[L2] *Katartizō* (G2675) means "to prepare, to fit."
[L4] The sign in Isaiah 7:14, as Matthew 1:23 applies it, is that a virgin conceives. Genesis 24:16 and 24:43 show that *almah* can designate a woman whom no man has known. Hebrews 10:5 says the body was prepared by God.

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. Mary was a virgin who had not known a man when the conception was announced. [L1] Luke 1:27, Luke 1:34; [L2] *parthenos* (virgin), *ginōskō* (know); [L3] Genesis 4:1.
2. The source of the conception is the Holy Ghost, not a man. [L1] Matthew 1:18, Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35; [L2] *ek* (out of), *gennaō* (begotten); [L3] Matthew 1:2.
3. Matthew's genealogy stops the "begat" pattern at Joseph and traces the birth through Mary. [L1] Matthew 1:16; [L2] feminine "of whom" (*ex hēs*), *egennēsen* (begat); [L3] Matthew 1:15.
4. Joseph did not know Mary before the birth, and his fatherhood is recorded as a supposition. [L1] Matthew 1:25, Luke 3:23; [L2] *ginōskō* (know), *nomizō* (suppose); [L3] Matthew 1:19, Luke 2:48-49.
5. Isaiah's sign is a virgin conceiving, and God prepared the body. [L1] Isaiah 7:14, Matthew 1:23; [L2] *almah* (virgin), *parthenos* (virgin); [L3] Genesis 24:16, Genesis 24:43, Hebrews 10:5.
6. Therefore Christ had no human biological father: Joseph did not beget him, and Mary conceived of the Holy Ghost. [L4] resting on Matthew 1:18 with *ek* (out of) and Luke 1:34 with *ginōskō* (know), with [L3] support from Matthew 1:20.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 2, RESPONSE

# Round 2: the seed is David's through the woman, and the begetter is the Holy Ghost

My declared chain stands. Below I answer the challenger's five links and the rows pressed against mine, in the order of the challenger's chain.

---

## Answer to C1: the seed rows and the loins rows

**1. "Seed" and "loins" reach descendants across generations.**
- [L1] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."
- [L3] Hebrews 7:9: "Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham." Levi was not Abraham's son but a later descendant, yet the text puts him in Abraham's loins.
- [L2] *osphys* (G3751), "loin... procreative power," is the word in Hebrews 7:10. It is used there of a descendant removed from the forefather by generations.
- [L4] Hebrews 7:9-10 gives a descendant several generations down as being in the forefather's loins. So Acts 2:30 and Romans 1:3 ("of the fruit of his loins... the seed of David") do not require that Joseph begot Jesus. They require descent from David, and that descent can run through the mother.

**2. Romans 1:3 uses a different verb from the begetting verb.**
- [L1] Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- [L2] "Made" is *ginomai* (G1096), "to become, to come into being." The lexicon sets *gennaō* (G1080) apart as "to procreate (properly, of the father...)."
- [L3] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." [Gr. begotten.] Here *gennaō* is the verb, and the Holy Ghost is the one named as source.
- [L4] Romans 1:3 says Jesus came to be of David's seed. Matthew 1:20 uses the procreation verb and names the Holy Ghost as source. The two rows fit together if the flesh is David's through the mother and the begetting is the Holy Ghost's.

**3. 2 Samuel 7:12 has a nearer son in view.**
- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:14: "If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men."
- [L3] 2 Samuel 7:12: "thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
- [L2] *zera'* (H2233) is "seed... posterity." It is a continuing term, not a single act.
- [L4] Verse 14 speaks of a son who may commit iniquity, so verse 12's "out of thy bowels" is first said of David's immediate son. Acts 2:30 takes the promise further, to the one raised up to sit on the throne. The loins rows establish David's line, not Joseph's act.

**4. Joseph's line is the line under the word against Jechonias.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary."
- [L3] Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel." Jeremiah 22:30: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David." Luke 1:32: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
- [L4] Matthew 1:12 and 1:16 run Joseph's line through Jechonias. Jeremiah 22:30 says no man of Jechonias's seed prospers upon David's throne. Luke 1:32 says Jesus is given that throne. If the child were of Joseph's seed, the three rows would conflict. The conflict goes if the seed is David's through the mother and Joseph's place is legal.

**5. Mary's descent.** The challenger says D3 assumes Mary is of David's house.
- [L1] Luke 1:32, said to Mary: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The promise is made to the virgin about her son.
- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli."
- [L3] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph." Joseph has one father there (Jacob) and another in Luke 3:23 (Heli).
- [L2] The KJV prints "[the son]" in brackets in Luke 3:23, so "the son" is supplied and not in the Greek.
- [L4] The two lists give Joseph two fathers, Jacob (Matthew 1:16) and Heli (Luke 3:23). Luke's list begins with "as was supposed" and has a supplied word. It can be read as running through Mary, with Joseph named as son-in-law. This is an inference, and I mark it as such.
- [L1] On Luke 1:36, "thy cousin Elisabeth" [G4773, "kinswoman"], and Luke 1:5, "of the daughters of Aaron": a mother's kin with a priestly line does not put Mary outside David's house. Mary's kin included a daughter of Aaron on one side, and Luke 1:32 places the throne of David in her son's promise.

---

## Answer to C2: "thy father," "parents," and the crowd

**Luke 2:48 and 2:49.**
- [L1] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- [L1] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"
- [L2] Both use *patēr* (G3962), "father."
- [L4] Mary's word is the household word. Jesus answers by naming another Father. The exchange shows two uses of one word. I do not rest Joseph's biology on Mary's household usage. This is the same pair of fathers as Solomon's, where David begat Solomon and God said "I will be his father" (1 Chronicles 28:6). The difference is that Solomon was "chosen" (1 Chronicles 28:6, "I have chosen him [to be] my son"). Jesus was "conceived... of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20).

**The narrator's own voice.**
- [L1] Luke 2:33: "And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him."
- [L3] Luke 2:43: "Joseph and his mother knew not of it."
- [L4] When Luke speaks in his own voice, in Luke 2:33 and 2:43, he writes "Joseph and his mother." Where Luke writes a word of kin for Joseph, it is in Mary's mouth (2:48) or in the family's act under the law (2:27, 2:41). The same Luke wrote "as was supposed" at Luke 3:23.

**John 6:42 and John 1:45.**
- [L1] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?"
- [L4] The row reports what "they said," and the verse gives Jesus's own claim in the same breath. It is the crowd's reckoning and carries no narrator's assertion. John 1:45 is Philip's speech to Nathanael.

**The word "supposed."** The challenger presses Acts 16:13 ("wont") against Luke 3:23.
- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- [L2] G3543 (*nomizō*) is "to think, to suppose," and also "to be wont."
- [L3] Luke 2:44, the same writer: "But they, supposing him to have been in the company." That supposition was mistaken, since Jesus was in Jerusalem. Acts 14:19: "supposing he had been dead."
- [L4] Where Luke 2:44 and Acts 14:19 use the word, it is rendered "supposing." In Luke 2:44 it names an opinion that proved wrong. Luke 3:23 stands in the same sense, in a parenthesis ("as was supposed") placed before "the son of Joseph."

---

## Answer to C3 and the question put to me on Hebrews 7:14

You asked: according to Hebrews 7:14, how is it evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda, given "by the house of their fathers"?

- [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- [L2] *prodēlos* (G4271), "plain before all men."
- [L3] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife." Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS."
- [L3] Genesis 48:5: "as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine." A father's house can count a son it did not beget, and the tribal reckoning follows.
- [L4] The house is Joseph's, and I grant it. He is "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4). He took Mary and named the child (Matthew 1:24-25). That is how it is plain before all men that the child belongs in Judah by Numbers 1:18. Joseph's naming gives the child a legal place in the house. Matthew 1:16 gives Joseph no begetting verb for Jesus.

---

## Answer to C4: "of the Holy Ghost" as covenant origin

**The verbs and the "therefore."**
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L4] Verse 35 is introduced by "the angel answered" and gives the means: the Holy Ghost coming and the power overshadowing. The "therefore also" follows those words in the same verse. So the title of Son of God here is tied to the Holy Ghost's act. Verse 32 gave the title without a means, and verse 34 asked for the means.
- [L2] "Born" in verse 35 is *gennaō* (G1080), "to procreate (properly, of the father...)." The one who comes upon Mary is the Holy Ghost, and the verb of procreation follows his coming.

**"Is born of God" (1 John 5:1) and John 3:6.**
- [L1] 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God."
- [L3] John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."
- [L4] In 1 John 5:1, those born of God believe, so they already exist and already have flesh-fathers. The verse is about someone who is already living. Matthew 1:20's "that which is conceived in her" is about what exists in the womb and has nothing before it. So 1 John 5:1 and Matthew 1:20 do not stand in the same position. Also, 1 John 5:1 uses *gennaō* for the believer's new birth, while Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 say the pregnancy was found "of the Holy Ghost" with no one else in the verse as source.

**"Declared" in Romans 1:4.**
- [L1] Romans 1:4: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead."
- [L3] Romans 1:3: "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David." Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman."
- [L4] "His Son" stands in Romans 1:3 before he is made of David's seed. Galatians 4:4 has the Son sent forth and then made. Romans 1:4's verb is "declared" [Gr. determined], marking out, not making. The resurrection declares a sonship that Luke 2:49 already voices at twelve.

---

## Answer to C5: the union and the "till"

- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L1] Matthew 1:24-25: "took unto him his wife: And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L4] Two intervals are stated. Before the taking, the pregnancy was "found" "before they came together" (1:18). After the taking, Joseph "knew her not till she had brought forth" (1:25). The challenger says "till" covers the pregnancy after the taking. But that is the very time of "knew her not," so the verse excludes knowing in it. Together the two verses leave no time before the birth in which Joseph knew her. That removes C5's third footing.
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24: "his neighbour's wife." The betrothed is called "wife" there, as Mary is in Matthew 1:20. Matthew 1:18 itself separates the name "wife" from "came together," so the name does not carry union.

**On Luke 1:31 and 1:34.** I grant the challenger's tense point. Mary's "I know not a man" is her state at the angel's word (Luke 1:34), and "thou shalt conceive" (Luke 1:31) is future. Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 place the pregnancy before the coming together and the not-knowing through to the birth. The tense order therefore does not give Joseph a time.

---

## Answer to Matthew 1:16, Matthew 1:19, and Isaiah

**Matthew 1:16.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."
- [L3] Matthew 1:3: "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar."
- [L4] In Matthew 1:3, where a father is the source, he is the subject of "begat," and the mother is added with "of." In Matthew 1:16, Joseph is the subject of "begat" only for "Joseph the husband of Mary." The verb passes to the passive for Jesus, with Mary as the one "of whom." Genesis 4:25 and Luke 1:13 name the father with the verb "knew" or with "thy wife... shall bear thee a son," which are different rows from Matthew 1:16.

**Matthew 1:19.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] "For" is *gar* (G1063), the word giving the reason.
- [L4] The angel gives a reason why Joseph need not fear, and the reason is the origin of the conception. A reason of that kind answers a fear about the origin, which Matthew 1:19 shows when it says he "was minded to put her away privily." If the child were Joseph's, the reason would have no work to do.

**Isaiah 7:14.**
- [L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign."
- [L3] Isaiah 7:11: "Ask thee a sign of the LORD thy God." Isaiah 8:3: "Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz." Matthew 1:22-23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled... Behold, a virgin shall be with child."
- [L2] Matthew 1:23 uses *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin."
- [L4] Isaiah 8:3 gives a child with another name, Mahershalalhashbaz, while Isaiah 7:14 names Immanuel. The sign is offered by the Lord himself (7:14) in answer to a request for a sign from the Lord (7:11), and Matthew 1:22-23 applies it to the virgin Mary. The two Isaiah rows can be read together without making Isaiah 8:3 the child of 7:14.
- [L3] I grant the challenger that the "neither had any man known her" clause stands at Genesis 24:16 on *bethulah* (H1330), and that Genesis 24:43 has *almah* (H5959). Both verses are about Rebekah, which was my point.

**Hebrews 10:5 and 2:14.**
- [L1] Hebrews 2:14: "he also himself likewise took part of the same."
- [L3] Genesis 3:15: "and her seed."
- [L4] I grant that the body is flesh. Hebrews 2:16 gives it as of Abraham's seed, and Genesis 3:15 names the woman's seed, which fits a body taken from the woman.

---

## Where the chain stands

1. Joseph's house, naming and legal place are granted (Luke 2:4; Matthew 1:21, 1:24-25).
2. The conception was found "before they came together" (Matthew 1:18), and Joseph "knew her not till she had brought forth" (Matthew 1:25). So no time of union remains in which Joseph could have begotten.
3. The begetting verb names the Holy Ghost (Matthew 1:20; Luke 1:35).
4. The seed of David is carried to Jesus by descent through the woman, on the footing of Hebrews 7:9-10 and Luke 1:32 with 3:23.

# LINK ROUND

**LINK 6: SUPPORTED**

Footing:
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080), "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)." It is the verb of Matthew 1:2, "Abraham begat Isaac," and it stands in Matthew 1:20 with the Holy Ghost as the source.
- [L3] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L4] Mary asks how, with no man (1:34). The answer names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, not a man (1:35). Matthew 1:20 uses the begetting verb of the same source. So the begetter named is the Holy Ghost, and Joseph is not.

Answers to the pressed verses:

1. Romans 1:3, "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
   - [L2] *sperma* (G4690), "something sown, i.e. seed (including the male 'sperm'); by implication, offspring." The gloss says "including" and adds "offspring"; it is not male only.
   - [L3] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed." The seed there is the woman's.
   - [L3] Galatians 4:4: "made of a woman." *Ginomai* (G1096, "to become") is one verb in both verses.
   - [L4] Romans 1:3 gives the stock, "of the seed of David." Galatians 4:4 gives the womb, "of a woman." Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 put the Holy Ghost in the begetter's place. So the Davidic flesh comes by the woman.

2. Acts 2:30, "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh."
   - [L2] *osphys* (G3751), "procreative power."
   - [L3] Hebrews 7:10: "he was yet in the loins of his father." Levi is in the loins of Abraham, called "his father" across generations.
   - [L3] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus." The chain of "begat" (Matthew 1:2, 1:15) ends at Joseph and passes by *gennaō* in the passive, "was born," to the woman.
   - [L4] The fruit of David's loins is reached at the last step through the woman.

3. 2 Samuel 7:12, "which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
   - [L2] *me'eh* (H4578), "the seat of generation."
   - [L3] 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."
   - [L3] Hebrews 1:5: "I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?" The apostle applies that promise to Christ.
   - [L4] The bowels-promise carries God as father beside David's seed. Hebrews 1:5 brings both halves to Christ.

4. Hebrews 7:14, "our Lord sprang out of Juda."
   - [L2] *anatellō* (G393), "to arise, spring (up)." It names the tribe, Juda, as the stock.
   - [L3] Luke 2:4: "of the house and lineage of David."
   - [L4] I grant the tribe and the house. Hebrews 7:14 is met by the legal house, which I hold.

5. Numbers 1:18, "by the house of their fathers."
   - [L2] *'ab* (H1), "father"; *bayith* (H1004), "house."
   - [L3] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
   - [L4] The rule counts the congregation by fathers' houses. Joseph's reckoned sonship stands in his house (Luke 2:4), so the rule is met without Joseph begetting.

6. Matthew 1:20, "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not."

## Closing statement

The conception comes after "I know not a man" (Luke 1:34). It is "of the Holy Ghost" and "before they came together" (Matthew 1:18). It is "in her" (Matthew 1:20). The register's last link turns from "begat" to "of whom was born" (Matthew 1:16). Luke 3:23 marks Joseph's sonship with "(as was supposed)," and Luke 2:49 answers "thy father" with "my Father's business." On that footing D1 through D6 stand: Christ had no human biological father.
